topic: Chris Hemsworth launches KINSYN, a personalized longevity platform

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Chris Hemsworth launches KINSYN, a personalized longevity platform

facts.label: Article
facts.value: It’s no surprise that Chris Hemsworth is into fitness. He’s a good-looking, sculpted dude. But it seems he’s just as interested in longevity. As the co-founder of KINSYN , Hemsworth is looking to shift the focus from simply living longer to living better for longer. Chris Hemsworth is betting on a more personalized future for health and longevity. The platform brings together health history, bloodwork, wearable data, and individual goals to help build a more complete picture of your health. From everyday supplements and performance support to physician-guided treatments for weight management, skin, and hair health, KINSYN aims to make wellness a little less one-size-fits-all. Since everyone’s health needs are different, KINSYN offers several ways to build a more personalized wellness routine. At the most personalized level, KINSYN starts with a Comprehensive Biomarker Panel, administered at a lab or by a licensed phlebotomist in the comfort of your own home. By testing more than 50 biomarkers across metabolic, cardiovascular, thyroid, hormone, inflammation, stress, iron, and nutrient status, the test provides a more detailed view of what supplements may best support your health right now. KINSYN also incorporates wearable data collected from your watch, ring, or fitness tracker.

en.headline: Chris Hemsworth launches KINSYN, a personalized longevity platform

topic: Crunch Fitness Introduces a New Training Zone with Specialty Equipment and a Space to Create, Share and Connect

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Crunch Fitness Introduces a New Training Zone with Specialty Equipment and a Space to Create, Share and Connect

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Crunch Fitness announced a new immersive training zone built for total body workouts, featuring a curated selection of specialty equipment, a community turf area, and a semi-private space for members who want to create content and connect with others pursuing their own goals. The first two pilots will open in February at Crunch Paradise Valley in Paradise Valley, Arizona, and Crunch St. Cloud in St. Cloud, Florida, both operated by CR Fitness Holdings. The 3,500-plus square-foot dedicated zone has an immersive, bold industrial feel built for total body workouts and more competitive training. Members step through a portal from the main gym floor into a space with its own look, lighting and music, with design that nods to Crunch’s New York roots. At the center is a curated selection of specialty strength equipment, supported by a cardio and stretching area and a community turf area designed for gathering and training together. Members bring their own goals and their own workouts, and train alongside others doing the same. “Our members have told us they want more than a place to work out,” said John Tate, the EVP of experience at Crunch Fitness. “They want somewhere that feels elevated and energizing, where everyone’s chasing their own goals and pushing past their limits alongside each other.

topic: Nike to Sell $2,199 Smart Strength Trainer as Performance Push Continues

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Nike to Sell $2,199 Smart Strength Trainer as Performance Push Continues

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Nike Strength is bringing Beyond Power’s connected resistance trainer to its equipment lineup, another sign of the brand’s growing ambitions in strength and hybrid fitness Just days after Nike unveiled a wave of performance-focused product as part of its turnaround strategy, its strength training equipment business is adding something new to the mix: a $2,199 smart resistance trainer. Dimension 6 Fitness, the Nike licensee behind Nike Strength and Jordan Strength equipment, has partnered with fitness technology company Beyond Power to bring its Voltra I and accessories to NikeStrength.com . The deal takes Nike Strength beyond the traditional gym equipment that has largely defined its business, introducing connected technology capable of tracking performance and adjusting resistance electronically. It also comes during a busy week for Nike. The sportswear giant recently unveiled an ambitious innovation pipeline spanning strength training, running and recovery, alongside plans for performance sports to generate $4 billion in additional annual revenue by fiscal 2031. Beyond Power’s Voltra I is a portable cable trainer that uses a motor to generate resistance electronically, eliminating the need for bulky weight stacks. Weighing just 12.8 pounds and smaller than a shoebox, the device delivers up to 230 pounds of resistance, adjustable in one-pound increments.

topic: Seed Oil-Free Is a Selling Point

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Seed Oil-Free Is a Selling Point

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Health halo. Marketing psyop or legit science, consumers have deemed seed oils nutrition’s new enemy. Sans surge. Per NIQ, consumers spent $1B+ on seed oil-free CPG in the last year — a 72% YoY US sales surge driven primarily by salty snacks. On-label. Amid healthwashing, third-party certification is rewarding transparent brands, with sales of Seed Oil Free Certified foods up 18.1% YoY through August. While the FDA has yet to define UPFs, 300+ brands—including Chomps and Simple Mills—already sport Non-UPF Verified badges, adhering to tight rules around oil processing. Fat profits. Meanwhile, beef tallow is becoming the go-to oil replacement, with SPINS reporting tallow-fried snack sales surged 275% to $1.1B over three years. Better-for-you alternatives, VACA and Jesse & Ben’s landed funding, while MASA scored Target and Whole Foods shelf space. Punchline: Despite lack of scientific consensus, seed oils’ link to ultra-processed foods makes avoidance feel intuitive to wellness consumers — but fraudulent labels present a new problem. topic: How seca Is Making Longevity Measurable

facts.label: Story
facts.value: How seca Is Making Longevity Measurable

facts.label: Article
facts.value: As longevity brings greater focus to muscle health, metabolic resilience and long-term performance, fitness and wellness operators can differentiate their offerings with medically validated body composition insights and measurable progress Body composition is becoming a more prominent part of the longevity conversation, leading to refined insights on how muscle health and metabolic function contribute to long-term performance and healthy aging. For fitness and wellness operators, tracking these changes creates an opportunity to translate fitness and wellness activity into tangible results and demonstrate their programming’s value. James LaValle, RPh, CCN, is an internationally recognized clinical pharmacist, board-certified clinical nutritionist, author and educator with more than 40 years of experience in metabolic health, integrative care and longevity medicine. His view of performance aging shifts the conversation beyond lifespan and toward preserving physical function, metabolic resilience and long-term performance. James LaValle (credit: seca) For individuals, those goals are personal: maintaining strength, staying independent and continuing to do the things they enjoy. For operators, they raise an important question: How do you demonstrate that the time and effort invested in health and wellness are making a measurable difference?
